Hey folks,
This one is absolutely infuriating.
Jared Kushner is supposed to be Donald Trump's peace envoy. He's involved in negotiations over Ukraine, Iran, and Gaza. But new reporting reveals that his private equity firm held a $32 million stake in a defense supplier whose products are used in American fighter jets, warships, and submarines.
While Kushner faces serious questions about conflicts of interest, he and Ivanka Trump are developing a massive luxury island resort off the coast of Albania, where their plans have sparked widespread controversy and protests.
We're talking about a family that seems to find a way to make money from every crisis, every conflict, and every position of power they touch.
* [**00:00:35**] Ivanka Trump's Mediterranean island project, the controversy in Albania, and why I'm asking serious questions about where the money is coming from.
* [**00:02:20**] The $32 million defense investment, the weapons involved, and the glaring conflict of interest surrounding Jared Kushner's role as a peace negotiator.
* [**00:05:21**] Why the timing of Kushner's financial disclosure matters, what the reporting reveals, and the questions Congress needs to ask.
* [**00:08:21**] Protests in Albania, the luxury resort controversy, and why this family's business dealings deserve far more scrutiny.
* [**00:11:43**] The fight for accountability, aggressive congressional investigations, and the sweeping ethics reforms we need to make sure this never happens again.

What makes me angriest isn't just the money. It's the human cost. Families in Ukraine, Palestine, Israel, Iran, and here at home are living with the consequences of war and political decisions while powerful people face questions about whether they're financially benefiting from those same conflicts.
We cannot normalize this. We cannot accept a government where public service and private profit become impossible to separate.
And we sure as hell cannot let these questions disappear without answers.
If you care about exposing corruption, protecting democracy, and holding the Trump family accountable, this is a must-watch.

Not too long ago, I was playing quinceañeras every Friday night because my opponent said that's where I belonged.
I loved every one of them. But this Friday, I did something a little different: I sat next to Bill Maher on HBO's Real Time and talked about how we flipped TX-15.
**[From South Texas to Bill Maher's stage, our movement keeps getting bigger. Will you chip in right now to keep that momentum going?](https://substack.com/redirect/25226971-f904-4be1-a6f7-689bd6e6d729?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[CHIP IN](https://substack.com/redirect/25226971-f904-4be1-a6f7-689bd6e6d729?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/25226971-f904-4be1-a6f7-689bd6e6d729?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
I wanted you to hear a few of the things I told Bill, because your support is the reason every one of them is true.
He asked how much we flipped this seat by.
_43 points, I told him. On a map Republicans redrew mid-decade to make sure that could never happen._
He asked about the border. Donald Trump wanted to build a wall down here. Well, all border districts in Texas just went blue.
_That 's a big blue wall, I said._
Then Bill called me a blue dog and asked how I fit in a party like ours. I told him the truth: we're a big tent, and on things like health care, there's a lot of common ground to work with.
_Bill 's take? "It's a big hat party."_
I'll take it.
Here's what I didn't get to say on TV: Republicans know exactly how they lost this seat, and soon enough they'll be figuring out how to take it back. The map they drew to beat me is still the map.
**[So I'm asking you to help me start the next journey the way we won our last one: with a grassroots movement, one small donation at a time. Will you chip in $10 so we can keep telling our story, from quinceañeras to Real Time and everywhere in between?](https://substack.com/redirect/25226971-f904-4be1-a6f7-689bd6e6d729?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[DONATE](https://substack.com/redirect/25226971-f904-4be1-a6f7-689bd6e6d729?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Gracias por todo. Thank you for everything.
-- Bobby

body:
Nothing feels better than jumping into bed for a rejuvenating night’s sleep. But our rest can be disturbed in many ways, so we strive to create a comfortable cocoon with pillows just the way we like them, soft sheets, and maybe a noise machine to overtake aural distractions. However, there is one element we might be overlooking that contributes to the lack of Zen: the color of the walls. While the paint color of a room is intended to create ambiance, it can unintentionally affect our feelings. In the bedroom, where relaxation is the goal, you’ll want to stay away from loud and bright hues that energize, especially these four colors. | | | | |

body:
# [](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/35?t=1&akid=2606%2E791427%2Eu0VCsm)
Friend, my team reached out on Friday to talk about the importance of staying engaged for the fight ahead. **That starts today.**
Congress faces a deadline to approve a new spending plan and avoid a government shutdown on December 11th. President Trump has demanded $350 billion in new Pentagon spending that would help cover the cost of his stupid war with Iran.
**We have to make sure that funding is defeated. We have to make sure there’s not another taxpayer dollar sacrificed for this war.**
[**If that’s all you need to hear, add your name to my petition today calling for Democrats in both the House and the Senate to vote against any and all funding for the war in Iran.**](https://act.ilhanomar.com/signup/em_stop_funding_iran_war_pet_nov26/?source=em261122-1-180&refcode2=2606.791427.u0VCsm&akid=2606%2E791427%2Eu0VCsm)
**[ADD YOUR NAME](https://act.ilhanomar.com/signup/em_stop_funding_iran_war_pet_nov26/?source=em261122-1-180&refcode2=2606.791427.u0VCsm&akid=2606%2E791427%2Eu0VCsm)**
Friend, Democrats may not have the majority until the start of 2027, but we already have a chance to prove to the voters who elected us that we have what it takes to take on Trump and win.
The war with Iran is perhaps the least popular war in American history. It has caused death, destruction, destabilization, and economic chaos with absolutely no benefit to regular people. This month’s elections proved decisively that Americans have had enough. **They want it over and done with.**
That’s why we must act — not just because the war is unjust and stupid on face value, but also because the people exercised their wishes, and in a democracy like ours, those wishes should reign supreme. Not the wishes of defense contractors, lobbyists for foreign nations, and far-right war-mongers.
This is such a critical moment for Democrats to show that we are willing to fight, and so I’m asking for your help to put pressure on my colleagues who may be on the fence about taking up what will be a difficult task.
[**Please, add your name today to call on Democrats in Congress to reject funding for the Iran War no matter what. We simply can’t afford to give Donald Trump another cent to wage war and sabotoge our economy. Sign on here:**](https://act.ilhanomar.com/signup/em_stop_funding_iran_war_pet_nov26/?source=em261122-1-180&refcode2=2606.791427.u0VCsm&akid=2606%2E791427%2Eu0VCsm)
**[ADD YOUR NAME](https://act.ilhanomar.com/signup/em_stop_funding_iran_war_pet_nov26/?source=em261122-1-180&refcode2=2606.791427.u0VCsm&akid=2606%2E791427%2Eu0VCsm)**
Thank you in advance for your help today.
In solidarity,
Rep. Ilhan Omar

subject: A last-ditch request
body:
We’re respectfully asking [ ](https://ak.democrats.org/go/98055?t=1&akid=10364%2E22930333%2E94Zr9o)
---
Derek, in a minute, we’re going to ask you to [**chip in $7 to the DNC today.**](https://ak.democrats.org/go/2234?c0=em-dnc-november-2026-gfr.gb4rMu&refcode=em_20261122_10364_fr&amount=7&t=6&akid=10364%2E22930333%2E94Zr9o) We don’t expect you to give every time we ask, but we hope you will this time. Here’s why: **Tomorrow is our first FEC fundraising deadline since Election Day.** After this deadline passes, we’ll be legally required to report how much we’ve raised in these first few weeks. **_Everyone_ will be looking at that number.** That’s why we need to report a strong fundraising haul to show Trump and his billionaire buddies that Democrats are ready to continue our momentum, win back the White House, and elect a Democratic trifecta in 2028. But we’ll be honest with you: _Since Election Day, fundraising has been really, really slow._ **If we’re going to report a number that blows Republicans out of the water, today is the day we need to make that happen.** **So we’re respectfully asking:** [**Will you chip in $7 to the DNC today to help us show Republicans that their embarrassing defeat in 2026 was just the beginning of the consequences they’ll face at the ballot box?**](https://ak.democrats.org/go/2234?c0=em-dnc-november-2026-gfr.gb4rMu&refcode=em_20261122_10364_fr&amount=7&t=7&akid=10364%2E22930333%2E94Zr9o) _If you 've stored your info with ActBlue, we'll process your contribution instantly._ | | | **[Donate $7](https://ak.democrats.org/go/89866?c0=em-dnc-november-2026-gfr.9s4leO&amount=7&refcode=em_20261122_10364_fr&t=8&akid=10364%2E22930333%2E94Zr9o)**

## Plastic Surgeon Sentenced to Death
A Pinellas County judge [sentenced plastic surgeon Tomasz Kosowski to death](https://email.editor.joinflyoverflorida.com/c/eJykkLGu4yAQRb8Gd1gwYPuloNiG7m27pTWGIZldApFNbOXvV47yB68baXTvzDl_vudv5Mzl-hvv5FJNc6Fjy9QarXPKtUbaMTyxcS3bc71SxII8g4JRai0BZgyNd5otdtFN9gvV0pHT02Uw1l4u0N2cAb1QCghjUiaEYQFtBjMtIYRojLYdu7NPawCthtGo3savZUhTtBTtMKIVVlHkVtf-b-WS8qvutKZcV47Yh3rvsru19tiE-SXAC_DHcfS5BsxanXsB_sQS4D8hAf48KcBr_Z4F-EfGrXGQb8xaZKhl59AoyprkP86nJZnxeNEquchPk-RNblQalUBRtiojYbsJ8N3q4uM4Y9s4Cauud-T8frb90PPu4H8AAAD__1sGkxc) Friday for murdering attorney Steven Cozzi, whose body was never found. Prosecutors said Kosowski killed the 41-year-old in the bathroom of Cozzi's law office in March 2023, then wheeled out a "very heavy" wagon caught on surveillance video. Cozzi had been representing defendants in a lawsuit Kosowski filed. Kosowski represented himself, waived a jury, and was convicted in September. Judge Joseph Bulone found the killing was done for financial gain and was ["cold, calculated and premeditated"](https://email.editor.joinflyoverflorida.com/c/eJykkMHK2zAQhJ9GvilYa8lyDjoUim9_L6X0aDbedbJFloKkJOTti0PfoKc5zDDMN7-_li-UKOn6A3cOW96WxK8auTUuyxZzJn7i-sAmOdVHuTJhQlmgh1EbowEWXJs8ebHYUfB2wv7ScTD-7AZrz2foboGAwdOEDkfTkz0zOUM0GbKGvHHcSTj6jAEwvRuH_mRpurjNk2WybkSrbM8kLZfTnyxpi-_85LLFXITwtOa9i-HW2r2q4ZuCWcGMl_XgODwF86-fCuZ_cX2PWJus-kOTk66cGqeVSRNju-n9UYiLpKvepdZDI77eXBTMteXyVsMspIbvZpgG8Na7rgS6vyRGqaNXtr_uKPGzqv3noc8AfwMAAP__uFKMDA). _"The defendant, under the laws of the state of Florida, has forfeited his right to live,"_ Bulone said. At trial, Kosowski called the state's theory "impossible," pointing to transactions on Cozzi's credit card in the weeks after he vanished. He'll receive a public defender if he appeals.

Danny Britt after Democrat Catina Hamm conceded, keeping Republicans' 26-24 majority in the state Senate. Britt led by 268 votes on Election Night in District 24, which covers Robeson, Hoke, and Scotland counties. trimmed that to 228, and Hamm on Nov. 13. Hamm said her campaign competed in a district "drawn by Republicans to favor themselves." Britt, who carried his native Robeson but lost the other two counties, pledged to get to know Hoke and Scotland voters better before 2028. A Hamm win would have split the chamber 25-25, with Democratic Lt. Gov. Rachel Hunt breaking ties. Democrats did flip the state House for the first time since 2010, setting up a divided legislature in January. Feds Plan $33.2M for WNC Biotech The U.S. Economic Development Administration plans to award to build a life sciences hub in Caldwell and Burke counties as part of Hurricane Helene recovery. The money would fund at Caldwell Community College and Technical Institute, plus water lines for Burke County's Great Meadows Industrial Site. RTI International and the North Carolina Biotechnology Center will coordinate the eight-partner effort. Partners have committed another $18.8 million. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick said startups "will now have a place to grow and workers a path to careers in medical technology." Republican Sen. Ted Budd announced the grant Thursday. Democratic Gov. Josh Stein said his administration has backed more than 20 EDA applications and will "keep working to bring back every dollar we can for western North Carolina." The coalition argues a combined railroad would leave farmers and other shippers with fewer routes and less bargaining power. ## Tennessee Revenues Exceed Budget Estimates
Tennessee collected [$1.9 billion in taxes in October](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJykkM1qhDAURp8m7pTcm_iTRRYt1N10UQpdytXc0TBOFJPR6dsXC32Cbr7Vxzlwvi7dhfzsw_hOd7YpXbvAR5w5Jd66ePO0MS0rhxj48ANvPtwouA4lVjlAjtjRkPzOnabM2R7BkB4ytlCbUumyljKb7ECqN7IyyiCoUgOWpKR2AAhcGwmZtycQABFANtAUTdPXdQN976TqTemElux8WrYiTZw4BI6R-Tp_LztvxbDcs9lOKa1RqBeBrcD2OI5imCglCssyUjhPAtvTI7AFOMcIbEusVK0Ftp9_1PyDdw4Pjvnbc2B2-evDjZwKiusz26xbDz_PPla10HK8k59__emf8XaLPwEAAP__55eBRA), $299.3 million more than the same month last year and $292 million more than the state budgeted. [Corporate franchise and excise taxes](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJyk0D2O5CAUBODT4MwWvwYCgk2c9aYbWg94bqPGuBeYtub2o55gLjD5V6VS_butN0g5lftfOND1vq0Fr5axd6xreySoCOcTSyt4pYA1lQeUuHLK55GxkfMVQk8vXCUM0XnOLMgwoGPaKiGVpnTYnVAeUAnQmoLeouBaaK1hlsHMKjI1JPcuZIxzxqhhZjLGa22Y95EKb1UkkmJM_axT37FjKdga4pY_zxfWKZzHkN3e-7MR8YfwhfDluq63DVg61vb_Ayq-HeHLT5zwBWpPIeNqmGcBqBot3eZRSrSjYVscqbWzZSiih3na-5GJWGCoLj6vlHNqsyaS3g9I-XtE_-WDL8e_AgAA__8JJ4QB) did the heavy lifting, coming in more than $220 million over estimates. Sales taxes beat projections by $75.9 million, and collections from August through October are $682.5 million ahead of budget. The State Funding Board sets [revenue estimates for fiscal 2028](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJykkLGupiAUhJ9GOw2g_mhBsY3d3XZLc4DD78lFMHCu5n_7jfsK232TSSYz8-dr-wKKlN6_4UDDHLaEd43IjGWr3wQFIZ-YasKbHBZK35D8poR6dVJ2Sm3gmC7cRmi9sUouMLoWjdTLNIyTFqLdjQ6Ls3aYtPAYZr2ACC-PTgUM8wQwtGSeQCmVklLMcu7n2Wo9S2u9GOwy-WYU6Ilz6XlHxpSwVsQQP_nC0rt8tNHszGdthl-NWhu13vfdf2DP-XEbtT6zGrWeORKTexAKk4v4YGVg7MJP8pTenc1QfHcWPKE8uuCF6Qc7JZQUYpiGfucjtsX486YYqb50M4r3ART_VeH__PEy6m8AAAD__8_jifk) on Monday, with economists forecasting growth of 3.5% to 4.49%. University of Tennessee economist Don Bruce warned the board that corporate taxes are hard to predict and could bring “very large double-digit losses” as easily as big gains.
## TBI Warns of Fake Kidnapping Calls
The Tennessee Bureau of Investigation says more people are getting calls demanding ransom for a loved one [who hasn't actually been kidnapped](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OpDAQhJ8GMiPb_BgCB5eQzaUXojbuGVqYBtnWWPf2KzbYDTbctLu-UlX9eywPoED8-gsH2pyfC2NJAXPGuKSdICKcF3JiLLRiJN6B_aKlHoRSQusF1kxvXDqovXVaTdCtNVplpr7teiNlvVkEo8BpI4e-n_oJeulGNO1oBjP5TkFN9jZUSmul5KjGZhydMaNyzsvWTb2vOome8hmbvGFGZkwJ8Rn-n2-MzXoedbBbzleq2j-Vnis9l1Kaske-n5We71aVnr9Q8eOwk2e4LuKXSCscSZws8oYiUkJBLL6V2ZEoEPnm62j9VSgESoOpOvk6gMJnoPzLNd9WfwQAAP__FsCMLA). Scammers [disguise their calls with familiar phone numbers](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJykkDGupDAQRE8DmZHdeAYTEGwy2d90Q9S2G2iNsUe4F7S3X_Gv8NOnqlJV_fmav5AT5_U37jSJLHOmqyYSoWOub8aDsHwo10wXBzo4vzHHGTQ8lTEKYMYgfNJssY2TBzOiDS1NZhgfvX0MWrfb5LTH5fkw_bhYAoOj1wTW9Atp462LLU93oDEAxmhnXOecHwZnvI-69-MjNlZTZClHJxsJ5Uy1Ei3pXznp6ELZ2zRtIp_a9L8aeDXwuq6rSyVg6u9Bt6SB1zdQN2jgJZ7VhUeuqiyqBtwV57Okk_OqFnyT2koVXElVlr8oXPLtwkM4JJot2DGS7lV0AygbIihcnFMhwGii9c_Bj90me2qPKX4uTonrc2isXnfk9F1Zfvj3OcH_AAAA__-pxpW_), including numbers saved in your contacts. The caller claims to be holding that loved one hostage and demands money. Payment requests come through [Venmo, Cash App, Green Dot cards, or other methods](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJykkD1uxCAQRk-DO1Yw_sEuKNK427QprTGMbbQYLBjtJrePNldI_-l7eu_rvtwxxJD2TzzJMm9LoleNxExlqY-AhTBflGqiV3BUQnpg8gsoGKTWEmBBx-FJS4eNtyvoCTvXkNVm6tuuN0o1hx06pBV713bGTETGDAqU2aYRNPS975tg34daA2itRj3exnE1ZtTr6lW7Tr0XnSIfOJcbH8SUEtVKtMWf_KRyc_lsoj2YryraDwGzgHnL3-5AZkw57_ieCJjfbgLmmB1GATOvQdYDS0i7xEiFq8ybLOQosbyOnEhWh2dtivXXK8QY6mBEp_YTQ_yj8j-TPS38BgAA__-zTYI7). The TBI's advice: don't send a dime, hang up, and call your loved one directly. In one case reported to the Better Business Bureau, [a Florida woman got a middle-of-the-night call](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJykkD0O3CAUhE-DO1bw8B8FRRq6TZvSAvNYPy3GFhBbuX3kXCH9aGa-79d7eTtKlD8_3Y6mtbhkvGvC1rAs9UuuoDtOzDXjTSsWyl-XwwICRi4lB1jc2ujCpXddMB6kdv3aoZGTHlQ_TEJ0m5FxjHpU0xp1jAo0riEMsxJROK17BR2Zp1BKACnFLOfXPPtpmqX3QSivh8B6gYHaUV5tw4Y5Y62IMf05Liyv9di7ZLbWzsrUDwaWgb3v-9VoxxoL4lmw1ifGwD58DOwzyMAea2NglWRgvff8diVXflFpv13iXwrZnSflT-WuID8ybxvyQhUZ2K6YcN6UEtVxYr347I7Svy_tP0VeBv4GAAD__8oUiK0) that seemed to come from her mother's phone, with background noises suggesting a hostage. Several Tennessee law enforcement agencies have issued warnings about similar calls.
## Tennessee's Only Ski Area Opens Season
Ober Gatlinburg [opened its ski season Friday](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJyk0LHOozAQBOCnMZ2RdwMBCopr6P5rr0QLLImFWUf2Buve_pS8wnVTfZqZPz_zD_ng5fGbTh5V91m45MCqnOZ8eEpM8cWShYtfOXk5SLYZHd4tgEWcaVV_8dxQtY0LwkDNWvEI3dDemrZzrnqObr8T7HgH2And0MLada5B17plWPtur_z4AQEQAVwPfd33S9f1sCybuy1Du5nG8eY1plqfrCzCOTPv4W-8ONVrPKswPlVf2dx-GZwMTqWUulxBa70MTh_e4ATwzQanuHCyZ3yLkhf7XWjz4W1mylEs7crJFuYj2yyxnHR4eVjl88WJ9J042zWKenmzTW-xhdJpcKrSuL2KD8Hne2ca9zjJh28__c9zrxH_BQAA___3lpAD) with skiers, snowboarders, and tubers on the slopes, even as temperatures ran warmer than normal in East Tennessee. The state’s lone ski area beat every resort in Montana, Idaho, and Wyoming to opening day, thanks to [machines that make snow well above freezing](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1uxCAQBOCnsTtbsP4BFxRp3F3alNZi9nzoOLBgcyhvH10i5QVSj_SNZj4u2wV98PF4xwcZ5usWqZZAzJS3cveYCdNJsUSqfqfs4x2j20DA3EnZAWy4s3_SNmLrjAW54Li3ZKRapmGclBDtzYgRlLZ2RrtP2l0nUGpwNCwgFzejhNabFyglgJRCS91rbZXS0lonBrtMrhkFOc8p93wjphipFKJr-EpPyv2eHm0wN-azNMNbA2sDa621P1N1v3ED62tXA2uylLsDOfhoP_PR_WFdYcxcunL3XSEsKbbZuLP6EHyZVTOK44E-_JTxP596GvgOAAD__7mAf90). Webcams showed skiers on a thin ribbon of white surrounded by fall foliage. Crews spent weeks building a base, and the mountain got a boost when it picked up its [first natural snowfall of the season](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJykkbGunDAQRb8GOq_sWQOmoEhD99KmRGM8LKNn7JU9C8rfR7xfSH2PjnR0_3wtX8iR0-s3HjSJbEuiq0YSobLUb8ZCmN-UaqKLVyqcvjGFBTT0yhgFsOAqfNJisQ2TBzOiXVuazDB2T9sNWrf7NOCmO6_dqNenD32v0ZkAQA784IN2LU-30BgAY7Qz7uGcHwZnvA_66ccuNFZTYMnlITsJpUS1Em3xbz6pPNZ8tHHaRd61ef5qYG5gvq7rZo_8SYKc3oVqvcEGZv-pfAsamLOnol4okZP_lJcqtBKfVNXGpYpKKJ-CUdWUrw1jVHlTP-kwqIuTUFGVsOakcCcM95zyqUA3MGMRXiMtG4z9CgMp2z071XW9U-NmrLLao7Oms5t2j12O2JYpvC-OkWs_NFa_DuT40yb_ecw5wb8AAAD__xhMoyo) on Nov. 14. Local skier Robert Pack, who counts down the days to the opener, called it one of the warmest he’s seen but didn’t mind:_“I actually kind of prefer it, because you don’t have to layer up.”_ A local snowboarder said it felt like 80 degrees and was ready for short sleeves.

## Raffensperger Certifies Election Results
Secretary of State Brad Raffensperger [certified the Nov. 3 general election results](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJyk0D2O6yAQB_DT4A4LxjhxCorXuMtrt7QmeCCjJcaCWUd7-1VWygn2Av-P38d1uSJn3tJ_fJCXFJeNni2TCNWFMgXhsrVAVTgyrfXYsX7GBQyctLUaYMEgfNDisFv9YFayburI2_NlHNw4gevu3k6AMLoT4I2MmeJgwaxhoNGNl0ucsGP_CrQWwFprAPop3NZxwOCQMJwjKWdoZSm1lzslKjUxxvxdDqp9KI8u-7vI3tTwT8GsYA64s5Ssb4TSl5oUzK8GBbO1CmaWpkuMHBizrhgjbW2nmqjq99Wmt3LoQb8NdKX2laUpmLvq1_3JOXM7nZUz6YGcf2fIHwUPDz8BAAD__-bKho8) Friday, making Democrats' wins for governor, U.S. Senate, and other statewide offices official. Counties had just finished [a record audit](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJykkLGuozAQRb_GdEZ4MIEULrahy7Zbook9kNEajOwJaP9-RfTeF7xmmrk6uvf8eUwP5Mjb8htXcrLM00ZniSRCeaJIXjhtxVMWnplCPnbMf-cJGrhpYzTAhF74oMliFVzbBDJ2qMiZ_t61thvAVi9nzLOBDpsBbjRbIPQt2BaDB2MH22PF7gIaA2CMaQDqwT9D16K3SOj7mZRtKLCkXMuLFkp5YZzjv3RQrn1aq-heIntR7S8Fo4LxPM_6zOG8ngrGi65gNOY6dwXjF0L7tO6RhIrO5FMOupAIb4vGd2DRn5nfFrRP28x5vbLlHaUoGKvswn5yjFxuvbLNsiLHTyP5oczDwf8AAAD__0N4iaY) of six statewide races and all 14 U.S. House races, hand-tallying more than 1 million ballots. State officials said [99.98% of the checks](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJyk0D2O5CAQxfHT2BmWKeOPDgg2cdabbmhhKHCpwbSg2q29_ahHmhPMBd7T7__vvt0NRTrDX5NQc_Dbie8akRnLhhEtUz6rxcLkCV25nqY8_AY9TEJKAbAZy3Thpkzr9NA7lGppUcv5Ng5qXEC1h_YT7LOC8SZ7M05eLnZyyk5qh0VN86xa0p9BKQGklD1At9jdjYOxyqCxs8dG9eiIc-n4wIC5BDI-_s8Xls7m1EZ9MD9rM_xpYG1grbl2wXQhXw2sH1ED60GVcyErzlfasYhC9SEiJWI6gzAvR1yFzaenksQPXeQX25ywtkW755tipDrNjepDMhS_v_mX2S4NXwEAAP__PLGE0g) matched machine totals. Gov.-elect Keisha Lance Bottoms will become the first black woman governor of any state, and Democrats will hold a state House majority for the first time in more than two decades. Republicans kept a one-seat majority in the state Senate.

## Virginia Reports Child’s Measles-Associated Death
Virginia health officials announced Friday that a child no older than 4 died after testing positive for measles, the [state's first measles-associated death of 2026](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkD1uhDAQhU9jOiNmMOxSuEhDt2lTogGPYRRjVtgL2ttHRMoJ0rzq6f18X4_hQRIkzp-0ss2HHyKfKXDOvA_PLWUK9HKSfaA5mbr69hLWacAKWw2gEQeashw8GCqc9WSYuoIt3LqmNk1nsFgsc3WrEbqxvU9guO08452gGn3dIFFTiL3yABDhkqp07QhdM0HL7IAIlKnYSd72Mi98yD5LFPLhvR28l9O2FsEuOT-Tqj8U9gr78zzLOE4npUXinLd4uRT21zmF_cIU8qKwf2-vOOtpkeC0E05683plSoGTlqj_qhT2Bu5tXYPCvtite54SgqT2pkw1ryThd0X-J8DD4k8AAAD__3VNhSI). The health department won't say where the child lived or whether the child was vaccinated, citing the family's privacy. The death comes days after the U.S. [lost the measles-elimination status](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOpDAQRL8GMhDdGGYcOLiEbC69EDW4Da0zA7L74PbvV6y0X7BJSaWS6qnqz2t8kUR5L79pY6dnGN985ciqnMZjz0qR_nnREGnJpm3-BonbPGKDfQVQIY40q5w8Giq9C2SYbMkOHrZrTWcNlqsLk3l0FrCZGM3TNwzPdgKP1qC1nqAUd_cBIMItTe37CWw3Q8_sgQgK07AX3VOtK5-SFnkLhfixn5zqed_K6FbVIxftrwKHAofruuqw_-_8fMcFDveqAocgKWu1MeXIuUocSdlXnknXKvGxp9t-A6p5lejL5PxxSYyS-0dhmmUjiV9Q_eFfp8PPAAAA__8KKIDS) it had held since 2000. Virginia has logged 220 cases this year, [more than the previous 34 years combined](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkL1urDAQRp_GdCB78LLXhYvb0G3alGjAY3aU4Ue2A8rbR6ySJ0gzmuLoHOl7fwwPZOF1fsOFfDnisNKZhUqhNOxbLij4GbhEwTnbVn9ElmUaQENXG1MDDDgVPmiwWAUf0RK6iry5u1trb85C9fTt2LmoRz1GAvxHzrUdUWvJEYYx6nvF_vIZA2Cuo5vQjcbdJtMRBYNolNUUuGypKU86OM28Mkb52g5KzbQtlfhnKXtW7X8FvYL-PM9mZ9nKtgqvdDEK-quioDfm9Svof1X1QpiFcp04U_2DVcmH_WQRzt1dWT0vyPKqlT8OdXj4DgAA___4MXuK) and the most since 1988. All 41 cases reported in the health department's Central Region since Oct. 17 involved people who were unvaccinated or unsure of their status; 33 were in Charlotte County. State Health Commissioner Dr. Cameron Webb [urged families to check vaccination records](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkD2OpTAQhE8DmRFu_DMOHGxCNptuiBq7Da0xvCfbC5rbr5grbFKqoFSqr_58Lp_Imc_tNx7k25WWk-6aqTUqy_tVG2b8G7mljFtV0_iVOB9hgRGMkFIALBgaX7Qo7KNPqAhdT15apyelnYJ-98ZOpDSlaI3EuLqPGOQY7ORSsuiM6tk_fVICyEfGIZpVOh2kIYoSUXZqpMjtVYa208Vl45Mx5e_XRWUIr6PPfm_tXbvpVwdzB_N930NYq3QPzZPoYH5sB_MVd7GWPYpWMHzxuQk-QyGsJPgUB2HNVMUPFbfvDmYsjUOmBVOUBgmEBdRC6SmID3CrME5Oymk9Adhhb0fui4_vm3Pmamynxu1Azj8z238-fHn4FwAA___d3Y8A) and schedule any missed doses. _"This is not a moment for resignation or blame. It's a moment for action,"_ he said.
## Postal Audit Flags $430K
Federal auditors found 340 employees at Richmond's postal processing hub had at least one [flagged incident](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkMHOpCAQhJ8GbxhgUMcDh714m73u0fRAo50FMYCaefuNk32D_9JJp_JVqurPa34BBdqW3xDR1NPPG14lYK2Y5z2VCgEOR9UHWIp-iL-eQrSzEqrnUnKlZrCVTpw1NM540Ahjg0YOY_fQ3ahVsxr57J8CJWonnBfdYEdAJfxTikFr6aAhc_tJqZS8j2hd_5ZjZ2WP6CSAZFqgo5pyW1c8KS-0EfjwSSfm1qbYBLPWuhf2-MXUxNR0XVd7ZbK3yNR0d2JqCslC4P-fTHaNaXP8KHvh6_HmGPeQPoiF2xQj1Urbwn2Gw90Mz7inXHlZ05dvsnH7RSFQ6QemxRKBwjdM_eGOp1H_AgAA___bBYnO) of leaving for an hour or more while clocked in. Among 139 employees with frequent or severe attendance flags, auditors identified 11,867 paid hours away from the facility, totaling [$429,973 in questioned costs](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkLHunDAMxp8mbKDEcMANGSpVbNehS0fkIw5YDQQlBtS3r7j2Df6L9ZN_kuXv-_UaX8iBt_kHrmTl9ONGVw4kQmncYxYMeDgWH3DOTa1_ew7rNIKGtjSmBBhxEj5pbLBw1mND-CzImu75qJvHs4Fisd37rbXrTN83DrB_G937XpMx2KOv6VGwve8ZA2DuoSvXvs3zMZmWyBlEoxpNjiWmShY6Oc28MfrwJ56UqimuRbCLyJ5V_U3BoGC4rqu6ZeZ5kWqOp4Ihs1BWMDjyeARRMHgO_zZxOlba5OZEe0wf-p_xprbUUJdQ_oSu2p1X9XDIOuZ4pIlU_X1aUOZdPp8k6_aLQ-DcdqrR84ocPkK-2O5p4W8AAAD__-qfjWA). Thirty-five employees averaged at least 90 minutes away per workday. The top six offenders were investigated and all admitted to timecard fraud and were removed from duty. Postal management agreed to four corrective actions, including tighter attendance checks and stronger supervision.
## Film Tax Credit Faces Year-End Deadline
Lawmakers from both parties want Congress to pass [a 20% to 30% federal tax credit](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOpDAMhp8mdEEkBGYoUlxDN9deiUwwYE0IKPGQ27dfZV9hm1-WbH3y9_97TS8gT2H7CwdavtcpYE4emTFO15kYPHwW4tXDlkzbvFfyh5t0o3uplNR6Asd042SgWuwKBmGo0KrH0LWmG4yuduv0OsOzM840rutmNXS9erYtuEE9224eKrKFp5TWqkRTL325cqpHXBSAEqbBhfiMNe94U9woEKz-67wx1u48Km935iuJ9o_Qo9BjzrnOe7rLUuix4IUelSpziZkuiEwJgvSQD3hjTPL6pF2uFMDLC1KCDWWxlXzLK57LxzGdQTL8lxQchqIt9FhFu1yZvKfUP4RptgPI_zzFv-zztvo7AAD__4jpilc) for U.S.-based film and television productions before year's end. The credit would cover [20% of U.S. labor costs](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkLGSnTAMRb8GOjPYmPdCQZGGbtOmZIQtgyYCM5YWkr_PsL-wjSrdO-ee3x_zBxDTsf6CHUe90nzgLYyqWOYziwLDZyRNDKv4rv2TiPcwu9a9jLXGuRmC0oWzhzqOCTzCUONo30Pf-X7wrt5G16Z3DOA89H4ZcAndkN6hA4s_Fmz7tqbx6bPWOfuctomvxQ59sC_EaAFs5VuMpLk0uuFFZaWDIPG_fGFpQt5rHjfVU6ruZ-Wmyk33fTc3lANLI3iAYrPmq3LTM67kvFduOguKmIKMIChP5uvfhMyMsH6iGDnzIbmYhU4oSgKHWYjZaDYoCguTbAZMwogF2DxqjMJfE8pDW7mpLmM8b2Imeb0r3647EH8B6zddX6P7HwAA___n8phj) for productions costing more than $1 million and completing at least 75% of principal photography days domestically. Bonuses, capped at 30%, would apply to certain rural, disaster-area, independent, multi-state, and onshored productions. Sen. Mark Warner, D-Virginia, said it would keep jobs "here at home." President Trump said Friday the incentive is "going to happen," but Rep. Don Beyer, D-Virginia, [said the chances](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJyk0L3OnDAQheGrgQ5kDzbgwkWa7TZtSjSYAY9ifmRmQXv3EbmFrznNKz3F-fMe3siJt-U3ruTlmoeN7jORCOXh2E_BhJ-JZU64nKZRf2dOaxhAQVtpXQEMGIQvGgyWk5_RELqSvO6cbYx1BsrooW2wt50btbVqtCpAa22n0YVeB2f7kv3jaQ2gn1H11I7a2aBbokkj6sIomlj2XEuki_PCG-OcvvtFuQ77WiYfRY6zaH4V8Crgdd93jXt6WgEvzMIh0fmE-K0kf9ajkpj3m7eluomXKNVIkbepArDO9EqpOsqayuyn4-aU-Gy7wqhlRf6vlvLDsy4P_wIAAP__Xvt9lw) of any tax bill passing during the lame-duck session were "pretty low." The legislation remains in committee. The proposed federal credit could supplement Virginia's existing film incentive. A [June JLARC review](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuhDAQRL8GOiN7bbi4cJHmukubEu3ZC2xiDLJ9nPL3ESflC9JMNZqZN5-38YYcOc0fuJKrxzQmepZItVIe961UjPgIXKeIczFafk8cVz-ChEEoJQBG9JUPGg22wU1oCG1LTl1sr01vDbSLM2g0kLd68helLBjQ9k3avg9ehjvplt2ZpxSAOkV2Ybgr23s1EAWFqBojKXDdclcXOjjPnBin-LMdlDu_rW10S617afR7A9cGrl8Rs-_-nN28HQ1cI6bAaRav8SeHWCkwCkxB1O2RuayCk6d0ApUOy95mF_Ynx8hluDRGzityfBXWf351OPgNAAD__7t-fsM) found Virginia accounts for about 1% of U.S. film employment and that its film tax credit provides low economic benefits.

## Smith Shatters Records in Devastating Loss
Ohio State’s College Football Playoff hopes ended Saturday with a [31-28 loss at Nebraska](https://email.editor.theohioflyover.com/c/eJykkT-Po0AMxT8NdI7GEzKBguIaur32SmTAs4x2gtHYCcq3P7HSFVdv48bPf97v_fkYPyjltH3-pgf3JmscNz40sxmXceOpkH7Rc1c2lTWJGhmbjN75AIjg_bgX0Z1nG7Fe-oavGLuae7x3t2sT8O7qtefQudB2cfYBHQXXTfPCUwjTbVqI5qlO_bkQ0XtEDK67EE7O4R1bFxpP7bVqHC_JpFxs5fORmN_y4nKZ5VHnfjXbtbr-qvxQ-eE4jgtnfvF2UClJip6yyg_nIHxbgChiE-Vc-eE8XfkB8SzhFrD9X6rPGLkoRHkWWyGLKkgEZVLZgAz-YYIrgm9BYkxzopzf8JXyCReSKeyZ3hIjrLKz1qVf9uPsarhXjft8UMrfZuzHKbx6_zcAAP__pvaf7A), the Buckeyes’ fourth defeat of the season. The Buckeyes erased a 21-7 deficit to tie the game in the third quarter, but Nebraska scored the next 10 points. Jeremiah Smith finished with 165 receiving yards and two scores on six catches and became the Big Ten’s [first career 4,000-yard receiver](https://email.editor.theohioflyover.com/c/eJykkDHSnTAMhE9jOr-RDBgoXKSh-9OmZAyIZyUGM7YC826f4b9CGo0Kaffb_fU1fXmOfLx_-p2cpLBNB90lkgjl6aA5-_LH_z0LSUmBUxEvJGkyYKxG1MZMZ07lpEUmrFbXUI3bUJHDbmjrxmIHVXBmbqGxfQ2LX2ltl7XulwGHufMAHQJV7B5BRGMQ0cLw8jgDYIc92Mb4vlYN0MqS8ksCPSBb_KSL8mtJexVdEDmLqn8oMyoz3vf9okgXHbfPmVMuz5ky4_OovyPoLSWZfYzKjI-1MiPiM2xr4Vl-U6adfdBlZwl6piXtVLQE0hvnIroBAP3xedWZFuKLsuZDz_zWQocOXCTlT5Xdet4cIxfbqQbeu-f4zSz_XfblzL8AAAD__y7flWc). Smith’s [18th 100-yard receiving game](https://email.editor.theohioflyover.com/c/eJykkL-SnDAMh5_GdN6xvBiWgiIN3aVNycggg3MGM7KyzL19xlelT_Nr9Of7pF8f8wfGFM_tJx40St7DfNJdEokQzyd5xvKJf65CUvIecxEUkjxbYzsNoK2dL87lokVmaNaxpSeEoaER-sE92w560-yjCbg43zuPjoJrzbL2QK1z6DHYYcUmjnUhgLUA0JnhgeCNgR5epmstvp6qNbRGyfyQnapISF_5TfxY8tGkcRe5inr-UHZSdrrv-0GJ3nTeyBwzl9qm7FQH9fcJOuQsHlNSdqpoZSeAGp1zQ6_s9JuYjoi7LkeUXXsm_Czax00LnZppybzqu5bgVcMY_YW86g0P0jnof1ALMhE3PK7XHVOKpetVa7YDY_rWl__--3u0fwMAAP__vwSZ3w) broke the conference record he shared with former Michigan receiver Braylon Edwards and former Purdue receiver David Bell. ## Westerville Breaks Ground on Transit Project
Westerville and the Central Ohio Transit Authority have broken ground on the [$3.2 million Brooksedge Mobility Project](https://email.editor.theohioflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGunDAQheGngc7IM3DBFC7S0N20KZENs-BgPMgedrVvH21e4fZHR5_-P9_ztwsxpO23O8kK74850atEEqE8J_LZlcPdVyEpvAcu4oSEZ9TYKwCFOF-Zy0WLzFCvtqMWHmNNFobxq-16GHS9W7dCPxKAJ2MMGTJd74fRfHUGFzNgWwf7OQRABIBej40DrzUMYHTfoTNt1Wlag3BuZKcP5BHf_KTcLHzW0e4iV6naXxVOFU7-LiFRKc2LilB-hhip4bxVOC0sTrm0qhjScRflM7lDbZnvtCpOqlWozhBj4KR8Zj4KrRupk32IQd7qyvyXFqlwqrNdr9dnWvqh6vR2uhD_c-THHZ8W_wUAAP__DW2LBQ), designed to improve walking, biking, and bus access in one of the city’s employment centers. **Good Morning!** On this day in 1963, [John Fitzgerald Kennedy](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DFuxCAQheHT4A4LBtskBUUad5s2pYVhWM8GwwqQLd8-2ig3SP1J70n_1225WYqU7p92R9NCXhKeNWJrWJanjVStxxqooMvpINcop5IXEDBxKTnAYl2jAxfZeRMQAVWHRur3UQ1ayLHbDFjnHcKoRzUOMDqhw-pHqeTqwts66Y7Ma05KACmVkKrXQU9uCMFbgUIrxQaBnlou_SNTahuGeOUDS-_y3kWztfasTH0wmBnM53n2G9WWy_VyBnPbqHJvL06J_wmDOeUD9xULB2AwP_KWeODfmBL6i9taba2UbEPfFeOfJ8VIddJsEPfdUvy9bv8Ldhj4CQAA__8KToHj), the 35th U.S. president, was assassinated as he rode through Dallas in an open-top motorcade. Art Linkletter mastered the role of radio and TV host over 25 years on his variety show _House Party._ As we learn in today's _[Whatever Happened To...](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkM1u4jAURp_G2SXyT2IzCy_QRGwGGCpUUXUTmfiaXDBxlFyS8vYVfYVuv086OjqnXbNzGLG_7N0dLIXU9LBMEYhgbAYXcXIepoAjtKmfsSVM_ZgayaXOhcilbFxLOEMjMm8DgASVgRXmT6VKw0WVdVaHyhu-MrqCs9dagOJOOtCiKhVUUmVoXzghpBRCcaEKE4xuyxC848CNUqzk4JHSWFwT9tRBiM80w1i06Z5F2xENE1NrJjdMbpZlKZ7pQY8zvP7X4qjtmNrMTNX_wxlEtXrczI1JHXEipurD9pAPx_Xl70Jvk2_F-368hnqLn6d_q1yHj2PNpMbewxdTdZmN1g8LxoiTNqzkl7vD-KNCvws4W_kdAAD__88Qgy4)_ section, he is best remembered for the questions he posed to young kids and the hilarious responses that followed. In case you missed it on _The Flyover Podcast_ , Ayla tackled the question on everyone's mind: why doesn't your money go as far as it used to? We ranked seven everyday costs, from the ones hurting your wallet most to the ones actually giving folks a break. Airfare, groceries, and gas: are you better or worse off on each? Where do electricity and hospital bills land? How much more is a meal out costing you these days? And what can be done about it? ## US Helps Capture Mexican Drug Kingpin
Mexican special forces [captured Fausto Isidro Meza Flores](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDGO5CAURE-DMyz4uI07INjEWW-6oUXDx_13MVhA2ztz-pHnCpOVVFKp3vvzWB6WIqX1t93QtJCXhGeN2BqWZbeRqvVYAxV0OR3kGuVU8gICRi4lB1isa3TgIjtvAiKg6tBIfb-pQQt5615mAv_Ud3dXw9NJqaYJJjUKVFbYW1DT1JG55qQEkFIJqXod9OiGELwVKLRSbBDoqeXS_82U2gtD_MgHlt7lrYvm1dpemfrFYGYwn-fZu2e9MK6ewXxFBvOG_8ll7st75f8orTslbkvB2niw79oyp0q-ZL7hp-Uh5oKVV0o2Zstg7orx-0kxUh01G8S6WYrfD9rPvB0GvgIAAP__NzGESg), one of the FBI's 10 most wanted fugitives, on Friday night in Sinaloa with help from U.S. intelligence. The FBI says the man known as "Chapo Isidro" leads a cartel that smuggles heroin, methamphetamine, cocaine, fentanyl, and marijuana into the U.S. Mexico's Defense Ministry said he faces a [U.S. extradition warrant](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkE1u6yAURleDZ0T82SQDBk96stRBOu3QuoZLcisMEVCn2X3lbqHjT_p0zvm4LlegRPn2Dhu6HsuS8dkS9o51eUCiBgFbpIq-5J18p5JrWZRQE5eSK7WA77TjIofgIqJCPaCT9jJqY4Uch7szqzXrBVHCCqjG1U7GCn_2woyXCabzQO64k1IpKbWQ-mSjnbyJMYBAYbVmRmCgXurps1Dud4zpVXasJ1-2Ibl774_G9D-mZqZmWP2hcGxMzW-5Y81wYENiat7wmzxk7qF2TDwhBKw8rtS4FPwJuWPg8etGhxRP1DpTc-ulvpieKTD9X-qzNpMUYqguPJ6UErXJMiNuG1D6Rep_C7k79RMAAP__qhaINA) on drug conspiracy charges. Washington had offered up to $5 million for information leading to his arrest. The arrest set off [a night of violence](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLHO3CAQhJ_G7jixgOF3QZHmukub0lpgfd4IGwuQL3n7yHmFvxyNNJrv-_VaXsiZj_dP3Mn3tSwHfVqm3qkuJ2ZumKitXCmW4-LYuRy1LEoqKwCEUgvGzhctMCa_EinSI3lw86SNkzCNm_9C0OFLqznIGMDYCay2JjljldSA08j-ngNQCkBL0A-3OhvNuiaUJJ3Wg5GUuJf6-F346But-W-5qD5i2cfst97PNugfg3oO6onnTXBXd6idY6ZBPXf6w7GIiLVTboKyiBueRXDjVItofGAuKC4umY5IwmkJwTqEAGF2JkQbkpJxTlLLSNKN1afzwzlzs24w8r0j5_-H-vc0Xl79CwAA__8ptIYC) in the city of Guasave that left at least 11 people dead. Military helicopters fired on key locations, vehicles burned, and civilians fled gunfire at a baseball game. Troops couldn't get him out until 4 a.m.
## Man Found Guilty in Palisades Fire
A federal jury on Friday [convicted Jonathan Rinderknecht](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGO8yAQBOCnwZ0tsxATFxR_4y5_e6W1hiXeHIEIkK17-1OuuBe4fjSabz5u6w05crr_xyfZFvKa6KyRWqOyvjByRU81cCGX08GucU4lrzDC1EvZA6zoGh-0ys7bQASkOrLSzBelzSgv3W5hMvOMwUzbJDeplJ6vjgI49JrQXLeO7btOSgAp1SjVYIKZnA7B40ijUUrokTy3XIZH5tR2CvErH1QGl59dtHtrryrUPwGLgOU8zyFtLuaK6U6R6jslYHm7BCwxO4wCll9bj6Xm1LfCGPtHTth2TH3h5Kl8JnJ7E7Co2YCetYClK9a_To6R62SEHu9P5PgzpP3tvsPCdwAAAP__AACF2Q) of deliberately starting what became the Palisades Fire, which killed 12 people in January 2025. His first trial ended in a mistrial in June when jurors deadlocked 10-2 in favor of acquittal. Prosecutors said Rinderknecht, 30, a former Uber driver, set a brush fire on New Year's Day that smoldered underground until Santa Ana winds whipped it into the most destructive wildfire in Los Angeles history six days later. The defense argued fireworks may have sparked it. [Sentencing is set](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGS3CAQRL8GZWzBoBN7AYETZefUoQrBIM0agQrNamv99S458A9c3F1d_d6vr-nLU6ay_PQbOk51Kvg6MjJjm3af6fARj0QNQy0nBaZaWp1AwSC1lgCTD0wnTrqLLiECmg6dtp8fprdKf3SrM3eYwQQzpxRCiEH1gw93DYOOszVx6Mhdc1oDaG2UNjeb7BD6lKJXqKwxolcYiWu7PSoVXjHldz2x3ULduuxW5v0Q5oeAUcDo52CvQMC414MFjI9aPK--yEYlYvtdMKwsU32WKJcnZX7LA5mpLHLO_g_KGYPfUP7Hlxe_jM92VRpyI58FjKDUoO6fIGDsmov7i3KmY7CiV8vmKf-7x9-Tejr4GwAA__9UlY4g) for March 17, 2027, when he faces five to 40 years in prison. More than [1,000 homes are](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL9uwyAQxp_G3hxxBwnxwNAlW7p2tDAc8VXYWHBy1LevkqEv0PHTJ31_fl_36e458_b49Cs5SWXa6NkyiVCddp-5-UgtcaVQtoODcNlqmVDhZQAYECcfhA-aoI8uESHpnhzY8ayNVXDuF3clQDQqmHEEmG262jkSnf1oQpwB557dKw4AEUAr0Ceb7CWYlKJXpKzWnVEUWUo9fRfeZKGUf8pB9RTK2me3iOyt0x8d3jq8vUbvpcnLfMvAicPw92VYWNoASqlhKSu1oYmvQrHDW19d3J-cM7eL7Yx6rJ7zu0T-h-Zw-BsAAP__4it5Iw) now being rebuilt, a fraction of the nearly 7,000 structures destroyed.
## List: Top States to Retire
Wyoming edged out Florida as the [best state to retire](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuhDAQRL8GOpB3zeG7wkWa6y5tSmRg99jIh5G9geTvI_IL6Uaa0YzmfTyGR5Ao6_M9vMgrp2Glo0RSpTxsIUoJMxWWTFNad5lU0prTgAb7BqBBHMKkstMA9eyZCMnW5MHdLrZzBi714id0FxxvaK7BXmfsR77ySNSBY-7NbazFn3UAiADWgG0du37qmOdgyDhrq87QLJpy-5lk1YU4_qSdcjulVx39orqVyr5VeK_wfhxHy-kb7HnkTFR4P-VphRhJl6-xGaloUzQolUZTk0klU539vB0So5TeVZ15voLEvw39H5nd428AAAD__8czebo) in WalletHub's annual ranking, which scored all 50 states on 46 measures of affordability, quality of life, and health care. The Cowboy State won [by just 0.01 points](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL1OxDAQhJ8m6Rx5Nz_mChc06Y6WMjLJ-rLgxJa9JLq3Rwc01LQzoxnN93qdro4D77cXt5EVH6edzhJIhPKUXODiFiqeM81xP3gWjnuOE2ocFIBCnNwsfNAE9WI9EVJbkwVz6dvOaOjr1Rp4wqV3YC6LNqabHZIfiAygAaJe12wfdQCIAK2GtjHeDHPn_eI0adO2VadpYYm5eY-8y0o-3ONBuZnjVge7iqRStc8VjhWO53k2H5wen34SFY6ZhDNttEuF4-pSuqs_0hsVUSm4mYqS-Osp3pWspD5Lne2STg6By2CqTt82x-F7XP6H7LD4FQAA__8EPILO), 61.56 to 61.55, ranking first in affordability but 33rd in health care. The Sunshine State ranked first in quality of life. Savings matter, too. A separate analysis estimates [retirees need about $900,000](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLuynDAQRL9GZKL04HE3UOCEbJ06pCQYsWOLESXNQu3fu7A_4WYddJ_qOr-e89NjQtp--h0cxzwTXDUBM5T58AmrX6FGLLBkOnFhzFTybJQZpNbSmNkvjCfMulldBDBgG3B6fPS2G5Xum5frQjAAX0uEvusjRLvo8DX0ELzW_WMNDbobp7UxWlulbTvGcVi6GFevQI3Wik7BipxL-zsj8Qti-uQTSrvkvUnuxXxUYX8IMwkzXdfVbjl4-oO0Fc9Q75owUwHGAjsQCzMdyRMhbcJMOxLu711WfyJtVX7yWxLAKjnLANKHBHf8P5dI0qckeyUr33Bhpqa49bgwJazDKDq17R7Tv2_8PaOnM38DAAD__7iAjns) in Wyoming and roughly $967,000 in Florida, compared with $2.2 million in Hawaii. South Dakota, Colorado, and Minnesota rounded out the top five.

**Whatever happened to Art Linkletter?** For a quarter century, American afternoons opened the same way. _" Come on in, you're just in time for the house party."_ Then out came host Art Linkletter, who had a gift nobody has quite matched since. He could get ordinary people to say extraordinary things on live television. He was born in Moose Jaw, Saskatchewan, in 1912, abandoned as an infant and adopted by a traveling Baptist preacher. He earned a teaching degree in 1934 and went into radio instead. _House Party_ premiered on CBS radio in 1945, moved to television in 1952, and ran until 1969, by then the longest-running daytime variety show on the air. [Here's what the show looked like in 1961](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGK6zAQheGnkbsYjWTLSaHiQkiXcGGLZSujjEbxLIoV5IlN3n7JvsK258BX_J_n8Rw483y7hDt5SWWcaVsyiVAdHyHzEiItiSthmVdG4TLXMhpt3A5gZ8wYUHilEZroE5Eh25CH4dDbbtDQN5MHi1eNe91D1Np1FmKPDhDhYFNAt2_YvzkAYwCsBtsOaXDYpRSDJj1YqzpNkaXU9rvwLBOl_Cor1RbLvcl-Enksyv5T5qTMadu29lWe8rzS-38vQXBS9rQqe5SvvTtert3Hf2yqj4-Nc-bFDarTt3vg_EvK30Ks3vwEAAD__-AZcYI). The format was games, guests, and household hints. But the last five minutes were the draw, when Linkletter sat down with four schoolchildren and simply asked them questions.[ Here's a collection of brief TV clips](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkEGumzAURVdjZiA_GzAMPPgqyqQ_aaqoStUJcuzn8BIHI3Cg2X2VbuFP75WOjs553-8NBRqvB_NAnXzsR9yWgCnh3E8m0GIcLp5mtHFcySaK4xx7wUWdA-RC9MYmWrGHzGmPKFBmqEG1lSwVhyobdMuRC6hM0xje1uDbRnBplVKgGunKMiP9xgEIASA5yEJ5VdvSe2c4ciUlKzk6SnEubpHGNKAPr7jiXNj4yIIeUpoWJj-Y2DGx27ateMVnel7w_b8Xk-zA5G5lsvvhLwhV87yrOxN1oCUx2R0_j_l0-rh-29LPxVn4dZhvvvukP-fvTV7736eOiZpGh3-Z7GQ2azdtFAIttWIlvz4Mhf8q6WsBVy3-BQAA__8CfIJ3). The book that came out of it, _Kids Say the Darndest Things_ , sold in the millions and was illustrated by Charles Schulz. Linkletter was also a shrewd businessman. Walt Disney, a friend, invited him to invest in Disneyland. Linkletter declined, doubting it would work, but agreed to host the 1955 opening broadcast ([you can see the opening here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0MFqhDAQxvGnibeVZKKrHnIoLUKhWygUepQxTtYp0Sw6q2yfvthX6PX74Hf4f126C3Lk-fqOEzkJqZtpXyOJ0NLdMPKKA62BF_Jp3tgLp3lJHWg4n4w5AXTohTfqTDa4QARkM3KmakpbVNqU2eh6LKkprffQIJZUDnVjsIdQa9vXfe0zdgdnDIAxVhubV6E6-yKEATXpylpVaBpY0pJ_J55lpBAfaaMl92nKohtFbquyTwpaBe2-7_kj3eXe0_EfC4oflW03ZV90__bZ_kyvz_iRLW647Rwjr-dKFfo6Icc_Uv4XYnPwGwAA__-6dXKP)). In place of a fee, he asked for the park's camera and film concession for ten years, and got it. His daughter Diane died in 1969, the same year the show ended. He kept working, writing 27 books and speaking into his nineties, and died in 2010 at 97. The format outlived him. For a quarter century, American afternoons opened the same way. " Come on in, you're just in time for the house party." Then out came host Art Linkletter, who had a gift nobody has quite matched since. He could get ordinary people to say extraordinary things on live television. He was born in Moose Jaw, Saskatchewan, in 1912, abandoned as an infant and adopted by a traveling Baptist preacher. He earned a teaching degree in 1934 and went into radio instead. House Party premiered on CBS radio in 1945, moved to television in 1952, and ran until 1969, by then the longest-running daytime variety show on the air. . The format was games, guests, and household hints. But the last five minutes were the draw, when Linkletter sat down with four schoolchildren and simply asked them questions.. The book that came out of it, Kids Say the Darndest Things , sold in the millions and was illustrated by Charles Schulz. Linkletter was also a shrewd businessman. Walt Disney, a friend, invited him to invest in Disneyland. Linkletter declined, doubting it would work, but agreed to host the 1955 opening broadcast (). In place of a fee, he asked for the park's camera and film concession for ten years, and got it. His daughter Diane died in 1969, the same year the show ended. He kept working, writing 27 books and speaking into his nineties, and died in 2010 at 97. The format outlived him. Two network revivals and every "ask a kid a question" clip on the internet trace back to those five minutes. Do you remember watching Art Linkletter and House Party? # Sunday, November 22, 2026
---|---
**Good morning.** On this day in 1963, President John F. Kennedy was [assassinated in Dallas](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0DGOqzAQgOHTmC7IHgiQwsVr6PLaLdHYnoAVM47sSUhuv9q9wl7g_6Xv67pcMabI63_cycr7lhemoyYSobL4nBKtRFxySjuxPB8h81P8AhqGkzEngAW9xBctpgnW6XAxDVkzXs5dP00wNZvVw-Xm3ZkG1G50vRuN09p0fYe9Dp3zTbQ_NWMADGgNQzsOwzSRR2dGMh1p1WsKUXJpZSOhN9Zb-uQXldbnvUl2E3lU1f1TMCuYj-NopW6YOUWmNpdVwbwhB5fzXcFMLCVSVTDfiZnC54S1Yq2RUWLmptjwOGJKsQ6j6vW6Y0y_I_mjz8vCdwAAAP__SFB8wg) while riding in an open limousine with Gov. John Connally, who was severely wounded in the shooting. Shortly after Kennedy was pronounced dead, Vice President Lyndon Baines Johnson was sworn in as president. In case you missed it on _The Flyover Podcast_ , Ayla tackled the question on everyone's mind: why doesn't your money go as far as it used to? We ranked seven everyday costs, from the ones hurting your wallet most to the ones actually giving folks a break. Airfare, groceries, and gas: are you better or worse off on each? New Natural Area Opens near Boerne Texas' newest state natural area, a nearly 3,800-acre former ranch outside Boerne, . Its namesakes, Albert and Bessie Kronkosky, began buying the land in 1946 and willed it to the state to protect it, and Texas Parks and Wildlife took ownership in 2011. ## Polis Seeks Second Flood Declaration
Gov. Jared Polis [asked President Trump for a second major disaster declaration](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO4yAQQL8Gd1gwBscpKK5xl2uvtAgMNjlssjCxtX-_cqSVtt9upJHevHn_btPNxhS3-a9d0ZAL04ZHTUiEZaro8uZDytl7dMkWSzFv93xMIKDnUnKAyTqKO07KNt6EAM72DRp5uepOgxa6Wczg7s6CEF64DsQglbJXIUIHsh-C7mUTzcmTEkB2QipoldeDFjZ0d7iCVoEpgT5SLi0t6HLKxfoc0mfesbQur00yC9Gzsu4Pg5HBeBxH-__haDi3DMaTz2CU8j0zGOe884ct6Pkzp1h5wY8XVqocNs9X-8iF-1htJSz8x-_8vMhrftFyYCX-7cLfkeI2MxibYvzziCnF2l-YEvNqY3pb0i8D7wa-AgAA__-39ZC_) Friday after another round of flooding in southwest Colorado. State and federal assessments [validated $28.5 million in damage](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOnDAQhJ8GOiO82PBTuEhDd2lTIuNdg0-Gvdg-UN4-4pRI6VOuVpr55vvxmB82xHCs3-1Opjg_H3TlSKVQmjM5PtBHZkRy0SZbAh8LXzO00AspBcBsXQknzcrWaLwHZ_uajBxG3WnQra430412GBcF0C-aNI5SjZq070liRz1-1cHceVICyK6VChqF-ku31ncLjKCVr1RLGAqnpmzkOHKyyD7-4pNS43ivo9lKeeWq-1bBVMF0XVeDdJyUhvtfwXTPqmCK7GwUf46VT_G0iVC8OIYsEv18Uy5ZwIFit09OAkO2uVAS_wgQd63I_C7bRbmIv0DiYyoca50Mvq4QY8j9UKl23W2IH87yn4pPA78DAAD__6GmlRI) to public infrastructure from the latest storms. The flooding also destroyed or left uninhabitable 271 primary homes. The request covers Archuleta, Conejos, La Plata, Mineral, Montezuma, and Rio Grande counties. Polis [filed the first request Oct. 31](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO2zAMQL_G3mRYlJRcBg1dsl3XjoYsko5a2XQlxUH_vnCBAtlvfQ8kyPfjc_oMKadt-R5W8i3ytNGrZmqNylQpyoacRRAp5lBCS7LN8ppghIvSWgFMIbZ00GRDj54ZYrj05PX15owDN7r-4Y2-sEE3s-HraBCdtfBxY4TAqGfiPvlzn9YA2ozawmDRfbgxsJnhBs5yZ0fC1KQM7UFRspSAwvmPHFSGKGuf_aO1vXbmWwf3Du7LaTYpVZhTpOH_zLDI8aY7uJ_vvhG1S05VFfr9pNqqWsPPExaqCWlrKWSFqYbaqKi3Juq5ZYm_FBNSCVnV575LaX3xuL9Szqlerp0dlzWk_O_g9sXWh4e_AQAA__8NXpq3); the state needed two because the floods were separate weather events. _"Colorado needs the federal government to approve both of our Major Disaster Declaration requests to support this recovery,"_ [Polis said](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJykkLGuozAQRb_GdI7wYEMoXGxDl223RIM9JlYMg2wv0fv7JyK9L3j1aM699_x7zA-MKe7rX9zIVhfmnd4lUa2U50KOdx8Ss_fkEmaskfeF3zO00EulJMCMrsaTZo2NtyGAw74hq4bRdAZMa5qndQRmQcCx82ox_WiUNoPuoLv7YQiDaaK9eEoBqK5VGm7am7tpMXQLjGB0ELolHyvnW32S48QZPYf0xSflm-OtSfZZ61FE90fAJGB6-fNzEDBdewRMiR0mAdPKpzw4xSKxvIqs-f92yMBZwl0aucWUIu8SQ6Usf5LkR0HcV-ljwVIpX8QmW3-8r4fSD0K364YxfdrUX4o8LXwHAAD__59riTI).
## PERA Board Caps Investment Bonuses
The board for the Colorado Public Employees' Retirement Association (PERA) [voted Friday to cap bonuses](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJykkLHO4yAQhJ8Gd0RmbWynoLjGXa690lpgSZAwWLBxlLc_JdJJ1__dSPNpZjR_btsNY4r5_ht3MuzClunVEjFT3Rq5kn1IpXhPLmFFjiXb8tqgh0kqJQE2dBxP2kbsvAkBHE4dGTVf9aBB97p7GEdkg_a0zIvVg70iTXMAv8A84DgTddF88pQCUEOvRriMXi-6xzBYuIIegxh78pFLvfCDXEmloi8hvctJ9eLK3iXzYD6aGH4JWAWs_5j2zB9fwPppELAq9dX_IfKgitIWrF6muEdu0pb8bPLAt4z5pMY7ZZaNMQQBa1eNP14xpdimWYz9fceYviP4h_-dBv4GAAD__3Xjhdg) for its top investment officials at 150% of salary, down from 225%. The move followed months of pressure from lawmakers and pension members after a [Colorado Sun investigation](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJykkDFvwyAUhH8N3ojg2WB7YOjiLV07Ws_wiFEJWEAS5d9XiVSpe5db7tPd6b7O6xlDDOnyiVcyzfo10aNGao3KWsnm5HzM2TmyEQu2kNOWHysI0FxKDrCibeFO64CdM96DRd2RkeOsegVKqG43inCclVJ6sr2m0U8ahB57MYhZSbGpLphXnpQAshdygNPg1KQE-n6DGdTg2SDIhZbLqe1kc8wFXfbxme9UTjZfu2j21o7K-g8GC4Pll6m39PIZLK8GBot4y_QH4QcV5LWh93zL6Vap8rqXkL5DuvCDUg05cX9LjmPC-KyhMli6YtzxCDGGqkc2iMsVQ3xPaf988W7gJwAA__-nrYZ7) found bonuses had more than doubled investment staffers' pay. PERA had paid an average bonus of $299,000 in one recent year. Board member Scott Simon, who also oversees investments for Colorado's firefighter and police pension, called the change "pennywise and pound foolish." Retired schoolteacher and board member Tina Mueh called it "a preemptive move."
## Colorado Ranks in Top Ten for Superstition
Colorado is in the top ten for [most superstitious states](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJykkLHO4yAQhJ8Gd1hmDXFcUFzjLtdeaW1gidFhiGAT3739L0f6n-DvppgZzTd_busNY4r58Rt3suzCmuloiZipro1cyT6kUrwnl7Aix5Lv5VhhgItUSgKs6Di-adXYeRsCOLx0ZNU0m9GAGUy3WWfQTzBeKbg5kHIK55E8GD3NZr5r7KI9-5QCUOOgNPTam6sZMIx3mMHoIPRAPnKpPW_kSioVfQnpf3lT7V3Zu2Q35mcT4y8Bi4DlOI4-lH-gTprTIWA5pYDlOy4r5r9NYpMhBt7kXhrL9npSbRw5lleTjZFJxizzB1zA0lXrn0dMKbbLJPTw2DGmzwL-4XlvC18BAAD__-V1hs4) in the nation, according to a study by social casino website ACE. The study counted psychics, astrologers, metaphysical shops, and fortune tellers along with superstition-related Google searches. It found nearly four psychics per 100,000 Coloradans and ranked Denver eighth among cities. Not every ranking agrees. An earlier [BetMGM survey](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJykkLGunDAQAL_GdCC82HAULtLQXdqUaLHXYMmwyN67U_4-uvzC60cz0vx5rk9MOV37bzzJiY_rRZ-aSYTKWsnzFWJmDoF8xoKS-Nr4s0IPY6t1C7Cil_Sm1WATXIzgcWzI6Wm2gwXb2-ZwSLOFOBkdg5_HcTZe-4d-4IZoNpq2JrmvT2sAPfTaQGeCfdge47DBDNZEZXoKSbh0cpDnzAUDx_yX31Q6z2eT3SFyVzX8UrAoWOrNRWq3kZz7-SUULHQpWLbMu4JFDmpPrtLW102lSpLEr9q-alsFhaqCpSku3J-Uc6rjpEy_n5jy_5j88NPbwb8AAAD__whhftU) placed Colorado second-least superstitious, though more than half of Colorado respondents said they knock on wood.

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/33f2fffd-54e8-44db-8a47-bc5f48cea4ee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Every year around this time, I try to figure out how much a Thanksgiving dinner costs, using it as a proxy for inflation. And like everything else this year (the stock market, the economy, inflation) there is a confounding collection of cross-currents. Bottom line, it depends.
The [American Farm Bureau Federation](https://substack.com/redirect/61d606fc-5c20-46b4-af40-f0b58f4abc10?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) notes that a classic Thanksgiving dinner for 10 will cost $58.63 this year; that's [up 6%](https://substack.com/redirect/9228a621-f4dd-4201-b69a-aaa99a3e16eb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from last year and the first increase since 2022. The [Wells Fargo Agri-Food Institute](https://substack.com/redirect/863eaf9b-28c5-4fb5-ac6f-f3b187f7306d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) says the meal will cost $78.93, _down_ 0.4%. [PwC](https://substack.com/redirect/688299ae-923e-43da-aa21-827c98a1b896?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) says it may cost the host around $90, up 2.3%. [Self Financial](https://substack.com/redirect/c0735d70-7749-4d4b-9f29-e71d5d2005d4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) says it's going to cost $137.93, _down_ 17%. And [Walmart](https://substack.com/redirect/40c0a9b7-2ffe-4a1e-9939-d9ff0b9c6c23?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) says it can feed the whole table for $35 (down 12%), making the cost per person about $3.50.
_**Navigating Uncertainty is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a paid subscriber.**_
[ Upgrade to paid](https://substack..iWBDHpXaDqgtqHZBiqfjV7UAmf4h8cFx_QJw5G5ootI?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=225877609)
That's a range of more than $100 for the same meal, in the same country, in the same week. One source says you're paying 6% more. Another says you're paying 17% less. If this is an inflation indicator, it's broken.
Last year, I made the same point. The Farm Bureau said dinner was down 5%. The AP said it was up 4%. The Century Foundation said it was up nearly 10%. I argued then that the contradictions weren't a bug in the story, they _were_ the story. Every survey uses a different basket of items, the baskets change year to year, and the results tell you more about the agenda of whoever compiled them than about what's actually happening at the grocery store.
* * *
## [Inflation: Time to Talk Turkey](https://substack.com/redirect/e2f61ea7-71cf-43f7-b070-4d6d740db722?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
---
| | [Vikram Mansharamani](https://substack.com/profile/37278065-vikram-mansharamani)| | *
---|---|---
| November 26, 2025
[](https://substack.com/redirect/e2f61ea7-71cf-43f7-b070-4d6d740db722?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Thanksgiving is a time of traditions: driving or flying to visit family and friends, watching the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade, strategizing for Black Friday sales, and of course, enjoying a turkey dinner. Another tradition, rumored to have begun with President Truman, is](https://substack.com/redirect/e2f61ea7-71cf-43f7-b070-4d6d740db722?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
| [| Read full story
---](https://substack.com/redirect/e2f61ea7-71cf-43f7-b070-4d6d740db722?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
A year later, I'm doubling down on that view. But I'll add a wrinkle. This year, prices are up, and it's not the turkey's fault. There's another culprit: diesel. The Farm Bureau's survey explicitly [calls out diesel](https://substack.com/redirect/9228a621-f4dd-4201-b69a-aaa99a3e16eb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) as a driver. High fuel costs raised the price of cranberries, dinner rolls, and just about anything that has to be harvested, processed, packaged, and trucked to a store...which is, well, _everything on the table_. Diesel hit [$5.97 a gallon](https://substack.com/redirect/e8bb6e21-4f0b-40b3-8391-2f6171896a84?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in September, a record. That's the Iran war, the Strait of Hormuz, and a global energy market in crisis, showing up in the price of your stuffing.
The turkey itself is up 10%, to [$23.68 for a 16-pound bird](https://substack.com/redirect/61d606fc-5c20-46b4-af40-f0b58f4abc10?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), about $1.48 a pound. According to the USDA, the price action is due to tight inventories and strong demand. But here's where it gets interesting: Walmart is selling Butterball turkeys as part of its $35 bundle, and some shoppers are finding birds as low as [$0.69 a pound](https://substack.com/redirect/61d606fc-5c20-46b4-af40-f0b58f4abc10?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (fyi: that's less than half the national average). Loss leader? Absolutely. But it's also the number that millions of Americans will actually _experience_ at the register, which is why Walmart can claim dinner is down 12% while the Farm Bureau says it's up 6%. They're both right. They're just measuring different realities.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/37225c6d-99e5-4a29-bc8b-2509a9f50bbc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
And this is the part that I think gets lost in the food-fight over food prices. Inflation isn't one number. It's a _distribution_. If you shop at Walmart or Aldi and buy store brands, your Thanksgiving is cheaper than last year. If you shop at a regional grocery store and buy name brands, it's more expensive. If you live in the Northeast, your dinner costs [$61.57](https://substack.com/redirect/9228a621-f4dd-4201-b69a-aaa99a3e16eb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). In the South, it's [$54.33](https://substack.com/redirect/9228a621-f4dd-4201-b69a-aaa99a3e16eb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The national average is a fiction that describes precisely nobody's actual experience.
_(FUN NOTE: I 'm often asked about how changes in average or per-capita GDP might change the consumption patterns of a developing country. Every single time I've been asked about how average or per-capita metrics impact an economic variable, I stop and invite the questioner to play along in a simple thought experiment. I ask them to imagine putting their left food in a bucket of boiling water and their right foot in a bucket of ice water. I then note that "on average," he or she would be comfortable. It usually draws a laugh from the audience, but the point is the deadly serious. Average can mislead.)_
[](https://substack.com/redirect/788a7efd-cf54-40c6-98da-3824f35dd798?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Meanwhile, there's a new variable nobody was tracking last Thanksgiving: GLP-1 drugs. Eleven percent of American adults are now on Ozempic, Wegovy, or a similar medication, and [Wells Fargo research](https://substack.com/redirect/863eaf9b-28c5-4fb5-ac6f-f3b187f7306d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) found that households cut grocery spending by 5.3% within six months of starting one. That's a prescription label driving a reduction in demand. When one in nine Americans is chemically eating less, it shows up in the data, and it's going to make next year's Thanksgiving surveys even harder to interpret.
So what does Thanksgiving dinner actually cost in 2026? Somewhere between $35 and $138. It depends on where you live, where you shop, what you serve, and whether your uncle is on Ozempic.
* * *
## [Three Dots, One Trend](https://substack.com/redirect/c989e534-ad9a-44b4-a56e-6cf4ed2bb6c4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
---
| | [Vikram Mansharamani](https://substack.com/profile/37278065-vikram-mansharamani)| | *
---|---|---
| Oct 4
[](https://substack.com/redirect/c989e534-ad9a-44b4-a56e-6cf4ed2bb6c4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Interest rates are on an upward march. The 10-year Treasury just hit 5.33%; the 30-year hit 5.69%. Those are 24-year highs. But this is not just an American phenomenon. The UK 30-year punched through 6% for the first time since 1998. France's 10-year hit its highest since 2002. The bond market is telegraphing distress.](https://substack.com/redirect/c989e534-ad9a-44b4-a56e-6cf4ed2bb6c4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
| [| Read full story
---](https://substack.com/redirect/c989e534-ad9a-44b4-a56e-6cf4ed2bb6c4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
Unemployment is low. But diesel is at $6, mortgage rates are above 5%, and the Fed can't cut rates because inflation won't cooperate. If you pulled into a gas station this fall and filled up your car, regular unleaded was actually _down_ from last year. It felt like progress.
But at the _next pump over_ , the trucker filling his rig was paying record diesel prices, and that diesel is what moves every piece of food on your Thanksgiving table from the farm to the store. Your gas bill improved. Your grocery bill didn't. Same station, two realities.
* * *
## [Stop Watching Gasoline Prices](https://substack.com/redirect/c26d939e-e3b4-4587-b2fb-098de27514fa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
---
| | [Vikram Mansharamani](https://substack.com/profile/37278065-vikram-mansharamani)| | *
---|---|---
| Sep 20
[](https://substack.com/redirect/c26d939e-e3b4-4587-b2fb-098de27514fa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[I run a frozen pizza factory in New Hampshire. We regularly have trucks pulling up to our loading dock with supplies such as flour, cheese, pepperoni, and packaging. And almost every day, trucks pull away carrying finished pizzas headed for stores across the country. Those trucks don't run on gasoline. They run on diesel. And the average diesel price ju...](https://substack.com/redirect/c26d939e-e3b4-4587-b2fb-098de27514fa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
| [| Read full story
---](https://substack.com/redirect/c26d939e-e3b4-4587-b2fb-098de27514fa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
The Thanksgiving data captures this split perfectly: a Walmart shopper and a Whole Foods shopper live in the same country but experience two completely different inflations. And that's why no single number (not CPI, not the Farm Bureau survey, not Walmart's press release) can tell you what's actually happening. The economy isn't one thing. It hasn't been for a while.
And for what it's worth, the pumpkin pie is [down 8.5%](https://substack.com/redirect/c0735d70-7749-4d4b-9f29-e71d5d2005d4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). How a family meal reflects economic realities. | | | Nov 22 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- Every year around this time, I try to figure out how much a Thanksgiving dinner costs, using it as a proxy for inflation. And like everything else this year (the stock market, the economy, inflation) there is a confounding collection of cross-currents. Bottom line, it depends. The notes that a classic Thanksgiving dinner for 10 will cost $58.63 this year; that's from last year and the first increase since 2022. The says the meal will cost $78.93, down 0.4%. says it may cost the host around $90, up 2.3%. says it's going to cost $137.93, down 17%. And says it can feed the whole table for $35 (down 12%), making the cost per person about $3.50. Navigating Uncertainty is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a paid subscriber. That's a range of more than $100 for the same meal, in the same country, in the same week. One source says you're paying 6% more. Another says you're paying 17% less. If this is an inflation indicator, it's broken. Last year, I made the same point. The Farm Bureau said dinner was down 5%. The AP said it was up 4%. The Century Foundation said it was up nearly 10%. I argued then that the contradictions weren't a bug in the story, they were the story. Every survey uses a different basket of items, the baskets change year to year, and the results tell you more about the agenda of whoever compiled them than about what's actually happening at the grocery store. | | | | ---|---|--- | November 26, 2025 | A year later, I'm doubling down on that view. But I'll add a wrinkle. This year, prices are up, and it's not the turkey's fault. There's another culprit: diesel. The Farm Bureau's survey explicitly as a driver. High fuel costs raised the price of cranberries, dinner rolls, and just about anything that has to be harvested, processed, packaged, and trucked to a store...which is, well, everything on the table. Diesel hit in September, a record. That's the Iran war, the Strait of Hormuz, and a global energy market in crisis, showing up in the price of your stuffing. The turkey itself is up 10%, to , about $1.48 a pound. According to the USDA, the price action is due to tight inventories and strong demand. But here's where it gets interesting: Walmart is selling Butterball turkeys as part of its $35 bundle, and some shoppers are finding birds as low as (fyi: that's less than half the national average). Loss leader? Absolutely. But it's also the number that millions of Americans will actually experience at the register, which is why Walmart can claim dinner is down 12% while the Farm Bureau says it's up 6%. They're both right. They're just measuring different realities. And this is the part that I think gets lost in the food-fight over food prices. Inflation isn't one number. It's a distribution. If you shop at Walmart or Aldi and buy store brands, your Thanksgiving is cheaper than last year. If you shop at a regional grocery store and buy name brands, it's more expensive. If you live in the Northeast, your dinner costs . In the South, it's . The national average is a fiction that describes precisely nobody's actual experience. (FUN NOTE: I 'm often asked about how changes in average or per-capita GDP might change the consumption patterns of a developing country. Every single time I've been asked about how average or per-capita metrics impact an economic variable, I stop and invite the questioner to play along in a simple thought experiment. I ask them to imagine putting their left food in a bucket of boiling water and their right foot in a bucket of ice water. I then note that "on average," he or she would be comfortable. It usually draws a laugh from the audience, but the point is the deadly serious. Average can mislead.) Meanwhile, there's a new variable nobody was tracking last Thanksgiving: GLP-1 drugs. Eleven percent of American adults are now on Ozempic, Wegovy, or a similar medication, and found that households cut grocery spending by 5.3% within six months of starting one. That's a prescription label driving a reduction in demand. When one in nine Americans is chemically eating less, it shows up in the data, and it's going to make next year's Thanksgiving surveys even harder to interpret. So what does Thanksgiving dinner actually cost in 2026? Somewhere between $35 and $138. It depends on where you live, where you shop, what you serve, and whether your uncle is on Ozempic. | | | | ---|---|--- | Oct 4 | Unemployment is low. But diesel is at $6, mortgage rates are above 5%, and the Fed can't cut rates because inflation won't cooperate. If you pulled into a gas station this fall and filled up your car, regular unleaded was actually down from last year. It felt like progress. But at the next pump over , the trucker filling his rig was paying record diesel prices, and that diesel is what moves every piece of food on your Thanksgiving table from the farm to the store. Your gas bill improved. Your grocery bill didn't. Same station, two realities. | | | | ---|---|--- | Sep 20 | The Thanksgiving data captures this split perfectly: a Walmart shopper and a Whole Foods shopper live in the same country but experience two completely different inflations. That’s what this season is really about, a divine rescue mission. It's Day 11 of the Daily Tip newsletter, and by now, I hope you've learned some great new tricks that make using your phone easier and more fun. Today, I'm going to show you one of my personal favorite tricks: the App Switcher. I used to waste a ton of time searching for various apps on my phone, but with the App Switcher, I can quickly scroll through any apps I have open. # How to Use App Switcher on iPhone
It can be annoying to try to switch between two apps you're using at once. Want to know how to quickly switch between open apps or close apps running in the background? We'll show you how to access and use the App Switcher on your iPhone so you can quickly view and close your open apps without scrolling endlessly through your Home Screens.
## Why You'll Love This Tip
* **Easily scroll between your open iPhone apps and switch to a different app.**
* **See all apps currently open on your iPhone.**
* **Close apps running in the background.**

## How to Open App Switcher on iPhone
### System Requirements
_This tip was performed on an iPhone 15 Pro running iOS 27. Find out how to update to the[latest version of iOS](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209627-5-0-262067-8633450-d995db1165-5t92d1693c)._The app switcher is a feature on your iPhone that allows you to easily switch between apps and close them if they are running slowly or not responding. If you like tips about using your iPhone, be sure to sign up for our free [Tip of the Day](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209627-5-0-262067-8633451-6d48c2cf44-5t92d1693c)! Let's get into how to switch between apps on the iPhone:
1. To open the App Switcher, swipe up from the bottom of the screen, stopping about halfway up.

|
---
2. Swipe left or right to scroll between your open apps.

---
3. Tap anywhere on an app to open it.

---
### Enjoying Your Tip of the Day?
If you'd like to learn more about iPhone Life's premium paid subscription, [click here](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209627-5-0-262067-3305294-b292827dc3-5t92d1693c)
4. Swipe up to close the app. Note: Apps only need to be closed if they slow or not responding.

---
5. To exit the App Switcher and return to your Home screen, tap above or below the displayed apps.

---

That's how to open App Switcher on your iPhone to view, open, and close apps. Keep in mind that apps only need to be closed if they are slow or frozen. Conrtary to popular belief, closing all of your apps does not save battery. It actually ends up using more battery since your iPhone has to use more processing power to open them again later.

body:
| Just not in the way MAGA wanted it to. For decades, Nixon's Southern Strategy, a silent majority driven by racist dog whistles, was the law of land here. 8 days ago, we doused it in gas & set it on fire.
---
_You're getting this message because you’ve supported good causes and Democratic candidates. We need your support to continue fighting for our democracy. We love having you in our network, but if you only want our most important email updates,[click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/108?t=2&akid=4043%2E259176%2EmaHf_L) If you'd like to unsubscribe, [click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/109?t=3&akid=4043%2E259176%2EmaHf_L)_

Nixon's Southern Strategy - a silent majority driven by racist dog whistles, was the law of the land here in the Deep South for nearly five decades.

**Only a few weeks ago, we doused it in gas and set it on fire.**

Now we’re finishing the job and putting that system out of its misery _by flipping a deep red US House seat in Louisiana_ on Dec 12. [](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/20209?source=SL_EM_FR_2026.11.22_PMoore-Southern-Strategy_B2_F1_S1_C1_180AC-360DON&t=4&akid=4043%2E259176%2EmaHf_L) This is Representative Patricia "Pat" Moore (D-LA). On November 3rd, the blue tsunami missed Louisiana’s US Senate seat by 1 point, but against all odds **I lead my extremist MAGA opponent by _0.73%._**

I grew up during Jim Crow and sadly I've lived long enough to see its return to Louisiana. We need to send a message and we've only got 20 days until our runoff to do it.

Missisissipi just elected their first Black US Senator since Reconstruction. Georgia their first Black woman Governor. Trump to stack our courts.

Schumer agreed to fast-track votes on Trump’s crony judicial nominees in
the lame duck. Republicans lost their majority, and Schumer is giving them
one last chance to lock in lifetime judges before January anyway.

Let’s be clear about what this is. It’s a betrayal.

The Senate has already confirmed 59 Trump judges. About two dozen more are
lined up for votes right now, and all have refused to say that Joe Biden
won the 2020 election out of loyalty to Trump.

Judges who can’t tell the truth about the last election should not be
ruling on our rights and freedoms for decades.

Schumer could have fought this. Republicans are almost out of time, and
Democrats could make them burn days on every nominee and run out the
clock. Schumer gave them a shortcut instead.

This isn’t the first time. In the 2024 lame duck, Schumer cut a deal that
left four appeals court seats open for Trump. Now Schumer’s doing it
again.

Deals like this only work when nobody’s watching. The more Democrats who
see what Schumer is doing and refuse to stay quiet, the harder it is for
him to keep helping Republicans.

That’s why Demand Justice PAC is making sure voters know exactly who is
helping Trump stack the courts, starting with Schumer. We have only a few
weeks before these seats are filled for life, and we can’t keep up the

subject: What I said on PBS NewsHour
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Voto Latino
body:
Our work in Texas proved what’s possible when we invest our time and resources in our community.
#
Peter,
I was recently on PBS NewsHour to talk about what happened in Texas, where Latino voters helped break a 30-year Republican grip on the state. I want to share what I said with you, because you’re part of this story.
[**But before I do, will you invest in Voto Latino's work and donate any amount today?**](https://act.votolatino.org/go/305?c0=em-ms-voto-20261122-1.EurD0K&refcode=em20261122-795&t=1&akid=795%2E1366028%2EM2Eb4L)
People like to say Latinos are not a monolith, which is true — until you come for our families.
That’s what we saw this year. There isn’t a Latino in this country, whether they work on Wall Street or in blue-collar jobs, who doesn’t know someone caught up in the ICE raids.
At the same time, our families are struggling to stretch every dollar. Two years ago, many in our community took a chance on Trump because they wanted relief. Instead, they got raids, rising costs, and a government that treated them like criminals. **And they responded at the ballot box.**
But here’s what made this time different: young Latinos showed up. For so many of them, this vote was about protecting their parents and fighting for affordability, because these are the issues impacting our communities the most.
Voto Latino started investing in Texas almost three election cycles ago, because we saw that 54% of the kids in Texas classrooms were young Latinos. We knew they were the future of the state, and of the country. So we got to work: we registered young voters, gave them the information they needed to cast their ballots, and engaged them year-round, not just in the weeks before an election.
Our work in Texas proved what’s possible when we invest our time and resources in our community. When you recognize people who’ve been overlooked for too long and give them something to vote for, they come out in force.
Now, we have to keep going, not just in Texas, but in every community across the country where young Latinos are ready to make their voices heard. That means registering the next generation of voters and staying connected with our community all year round.
**We can’t do it without you, Peter.[Will you chip in $3 or any amount today to help us keep investing in Latino voters heading into 2027 and 2028?](https://act.votolatino.org/go/57?c0=em-ms-voto-20261122-1.0VEIsw&amount=3&refcode=em20261122-795&t=2&akid=795%2E1366028%2EM2Eb4L)**
**[Donate $3 ››](https://act.votolatino.org/go/57?c0=em-ms-voto-20261122-1.0VEIsw&amount=3&refcode=20261122-795&t=21&akid=795%2E1366028%2EM2Eb4L)**
Thank you for investing in our work so we can continue reaching and registering young Latino voters for years to come.
Maria Teresa Kumar,
Voto Latino

I want to share what I said with you, because you’re part of this story. People like to say Latinos are not a monolith, which is true — until you come for our families. That’s what we saw this year. There isn’t a Latino in this country, whether they work on Wall Street or in blue-collar jobs, who doesn’t know someone caught up in the ICE raids. At the same time, our families are struggling to stretch every dollar. Two years ago, many in our community took a chance on Trump because they wanted relief. Instead, they got raids, rising costs, and a government that treated them like criminals. And they responded at the ballot box. But here’s what made this time different: young Latinos showed up. For so many of them, this vote was about protecting their parents and fighting for affordability, because these are the issues impacting our communities the most. Voto Latino started investing in Texas almost three election cycles ago, because we saw that 54% of the kids in Texas classrooms were young Latinos. We knew they were the future of the state, and of the country. So we got to work: we registered young voters, gave them the information they needed to cast their ballots, and engaged them year-round, not just in the weeks before an election. Our work in Texas proved what’s possible when we invest our time and resources in our community. When you recognize people who’ve been overlooked for too long and give them something to vote for, they come out in force. Now, we have to keep going, not just in Texas, but in every community across the country where young Latinos are ready to make their voices heard. That means registering the next generation of voters and staying connected with our community all year round. We can’t do it without you, Peter. Thank you for investing in our work so we can continue reaching and registering young Latino voters for years to come. Maria Teresa Kumar, Voto Latino

CNN's Kaitlan Collins asked a question **[clearly meant to drive a wedge](https://substack.com/redirect/668aa142-0bdb-4fa8-9f5c-b16a3637fd04?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** between President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance, while he was standing right beside the President during a press conference.
"There was reporting this week that you're unhappy with the statement the Vice President put out saying the reason Republicans lost the midterms was because of the Iran War," Collins told Trump. "Can you address that?"
Trump's response was just perfect...

* * *
# **Iran mocks Trump, unveils new dual-missile launcher amid threat of renewed US strikes**
Iran's IRGC released footage showing **[a new underground launcher](https://substack.com/redirect/3fb37a69-82e3-418d-9457-3a73137b4702?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** capable of firing two liquid-fueled missiles simultaneously, the first public display of the system, as commanders toured a vast underground facility stocked with missiles and military equipment.

| 11:11 AM * Nov 21, 2026 * 99.1K Views48 Replies * 440 Reposts * 2.83K Likes
---](https://substack.com/redirect/c3aa602b-807a-4a47-b677-b261a2bdb156?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* **The display, which included a message mocking the White House, appears aimed at countering claims** that Iran's missile program was severely weakened by recent fighting, with IRGC aerospace commander Brig. Gen. Seyyed Majid Mousavi claiming the country has added significant new capabilities despite the conflict.
* **The footage comes as Trump reportedly weighs a four-to-seven-day bombing campaign against Iran** alongside Israel, following fresh intelligence on Tehran's missile rebuilding efforts and pressure from Israeli intelligence chief Roman Gofman, even as Trump has publicly called the war "effectively over."

* * *
# **Iran 's president admits economic war "far more difficult" than military conflict**
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian acknowledged **[the country faces a grueling"silent" economic war](https://substack.com/redirect/05101fdb-acf8-40ac-955d-b4d5ed21a8dc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**, as Trump's Operation Economic Outcast tightens sanctions and a naval blockade, worsening inflation, energy shortages, and fears of renewed unrest ahead of winter.
* **Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Iran has exhausted its available seaborne oil supply** , calling the isolation campaign historically unprecedented and declaring "the ship is sinking," while CENTCOM says the blockade has blocked over $25 billion in Iranian crude exports.
* **Amid fears of unrest, Iran is deploying an AI-enabled neighborhood monitoring system** through its Basij paramilitary force following recent anti-regime protests, while Secretary of State Marco Rubio argued the economic pressure campaign makes further military strikes currently unnecessary.

* * *
# **ICE airport arrests in Seattle spark clash with WA Democrats**
ICE arrested two travelers at Sea-Tac airport Saturday -- Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza, a Mexican national accused of overstaying his visa, and Sofia Hernandez Mejia, who **[allegedly threw hot coffee at agents](https://substack.com/redirect/a9c86755-c392-46f1-86b5-cf84cba85a06?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** during the arrest and now faces assault charges.

* **Washington officials including Gov. Bob Ferguson, Mayor Katie Wilson, and Reps. Pramila Jayapal and Adam Smith condemned the operation** as chaotic and "un-American," with Ferguson urging airlines to push ICE out of state airports; none directly addressed the alleged assault on officers.
* **DHS defended the arrests,** citing steep increases in assaults, vehicular attacks, and death threats against agents, while Alaska Airlines said it received no advance notice and worked to rebook affected passengers.

* * *
# **Rob Lowe says Daily Wire 's anti-communist movie "Confession" was shut out of every film festival over politics**
Rob Lowe, star of "Confession" -- a film written by Ben Shapiro about Soviet-era persecution in 1938 Moscow -- said the movie, despite an 87% Rotten Tomatoes audience score and a cast including Nick Nolte and James Franco, was rejected by every film festival, **[calling the snub"all political."](https://substack.com/redirect/6f66c329-7565-4b42-af77-5c9355ddbce1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

[1]Justice Democrats

Peter,

Not even 2 days after the Democratic Party flipped both the U.S. House and
Senate in a monumental blue wave, Democrats on the House Judiciary
Committee were already back to making weak proposals on social media:

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20261122.jBZ3UX&refcode=em20261122-38444&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1002&akid=38444%2E1203867%2EktNOUP ]Tweet by House Judiciary Dems: It’s time for ICE to take the masks off,
turn the body cameras on, and start answering to the American people who
pay for their bloated budget.

The post got a ton of negative feedback, and for good reason. Most
comments communicated the same thing: abolishing ICE is the bare minimum
we expect from Democrats now that they’ve won power back.

Voters are tired of Democrats acting like Diet Republicans, as if it’s
okay for ICE to terrorize and hurt our loved ones as long as they’re
unmasked and wearing body cameras.

ICE is a rogue paramilitary force that has time and again violated the
rights of citizens and non-citizens alike. People made it loud and clear
in the midterms that they reject Trump’s gestapo and their cruelty: it’s
time to abolish this department and hold it accountable for the death and
trauma it’s inflicted on our communities.

We need to make it crystal clear to the Democratic Party: no more
watered-down half measures. No more mealy-mouthed statements and
‘strongly-worded’ letters. It’s time to fight back, seek justice, and
deliver results.

Thankfully, we have 8 new Justice Democrats heading to Congress in January
who are already speaking out about this and recommitting to abolish ICE.
